input: This capital appraisal examines a proposed bottling line and brings together the key financial figures that are relevant to the investment decision. The installed cost of the line is $1673k, while the expected net saving has been estimated at $350k per year for 12 years, reflecting anticipated reductions in operating expenditure once the line is in service. When these savings are discounted at a discount rate of 6%, the present value of the savings amounts to $2934k, and once the installed cost is taken into account, the resulting net present value is $1261k, which is positive and therefore indicates that the discounted savings are expected to exceed the initial outlay. It is important to note, however, that the savings underpinning this appraisal are based on vendor and utility estimates, and no saving has yet been measured on a comparable installation. This means that a considerable degree of uncertainty inevitably attaches to the figures, and stakeholders should be aware that if the realised savings turn out to be lower than estimated, the present value of the savings, and consequently the net present value, would also be lower than the values presented here.
target:
Capital appraisal of a bottling line gives a net present value of $1261k. The installed cost is $1673k, and the expected net saving is $350k per year for 12 years. At a discount rate of 6%, the present value of the savings is $2934k. The net present value is the present value of the savings minus the installed cost, and a positive value means that the discounted savings exceed the cost by the stated amount.

Net present value places savings arising in different years on one basis. Discounting reduces a saving in a later year relative to the same saving in an earlier year, because money available earlier can earn a return in the interval. The discount rate is the rate used for that reduction, and the same rate is applied to every year of the appraisal period. The installed cost falls at the start and is not discounted.

The savings are vendor and utility estimates. No saving has yet been measured on a comparable installation, and the appraisal inherits the uncertainty of the estimates: a realised saving below the estimate lowers the present value of the savings, and the net present value falls with it. The stated net present value is therefore a figure computed from estimates, not a measured return, and it holds only while the estimated savings hold.
